title: scoringProfile is a hand-typed label, not a fact about scoring: dynasty_main and dynasty_new carry the same string while their host scoring differs on 35 of 48 shared keys, so /api/data serves dynasty_main's board verbatim for dynasty_new
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Two leagues that use identical scoring share ONE ranking pipeline and ONE output... 503 data_not_ready only fires when the scoring profiles genuinely differ.' src/api/league_registry.py:480 calls scoringProfile 'the identifier for which set of rules produces this league's player values'.
observed: scoringProfile is an opaque free-text field parsed at league_registry.py:144 and never validated against any scoring_settings. Both registry entries carry "superflex_tep15_ppr1". The live host says the two leagues share only 48 scoring keys and DISAGREE on 35 of them (rec 0.08 vs 1.0, pass_td 6.0 vs 4.0, pass_yd 1/30 vs 1/25, pass_int -4.0 vs -1.0, fum_lost -4.0 vs -2.0, bonus_rec_te 0.0 vs 0.5), plus 48 nonzero keys exist only in dynasty_main (the entire IDP card, first-down bonuses, completion/incompletion scoring, reception-distance bonuses). server.py:3076 compares the two label strings, they match, the 503 never fires, and GET /api/data?leagueKey=dynasty_new returns the dynasty_main board with rankDerivedValue identical on 1092 of 1092 rows. The only test that touches the field (tests/api/test_config_parity.py:199) asserts the string is non-empty and not literally "default".

reproduction.expected: either a 503 data_not_ready for dynasty_new, or a board computed under dynasty_new's own 48-key full-PPR non-IDP scoring
reproduction.actual: HTTP 200, identical rankDerivedValue on 1092/1092 rows, meta.scoringProfile "superflex_tep15_ppr1"

numericProof.formula: count(k in shared : main[k] != new[k]) ; count(rows : rankDerivedValue_main == rankDerivedValue_new)

userImpact: A user who switches to 'Blood, Sweat, and Beers' in the LeagueSwitcher sees a full-PPR, no-IDP, 4-pt-passing-TD league priced with a 0.08-PPR IDP superflex board. Every trade value, every rank, every tier on /rankings and /trade is computed under the wrong league's rules, and nothing on the page says so.

priorFinding.note: Adjacent to PRIOR-A20-F04 (TE++ basis wrong for dynasty_new) but that finding assumes the shared-profile premise; this one refutes the premise itself.

whatWorks: The 503 gate and the leagues_share_scoring helper are correctly wired and would fire if the labels differed; the mechanism is sound and only its input is unverified.
rootCause: scoringProfile is authored by hand in registry.json with no derivation from, or check against, the league's actual scoring_settings. src/league_comparison/sleeper_scoring.py already computes a content hash of a scoring dict (_scoring_hash, sha1[:12]) — the registry does not use it.
requiredRepair: Derive the profile identity from a content hash of the league's live scoring_settings (the mechanism already exists in sleeper_scoring._scoring_hash), or add a startup/CI check that every pair of leagues sharing a scoringProfile has byte-identical scoring_settings. Until then dynasty_new must get its own profile string.
dependencies: Requires one read-only GET per league to api.sleeper.app, which config.py::fetch_live_league already does.

title: The cross-league Sleeper overlay stamps sleeperDataReady:true on a chimeric block — dynasty_new's real teams welded to dynasty_main's scoringSettings, rosterPositions and num_teams — which un-gates every team-dependent page
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md contract annotations: 'meta.sleeperDataReady — true iff sleeper block is valid for the *requested* league; false when the server served the shared rankings but doesn't have the requested league's rosters loaded' and 'meta.sleeperLoadedLeagueKey — which league the sleeper block *would* be for, when sleeperDataReady: false (diagnostic only)'.
observed: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, server.py:3244-3256 carries positions / playerIds / idToPlayer / scoringSettings / rosterPositions / leagueSettings forward from the LOADED league and lays the requested league's overlay (teams, trades, waivers) on top, then unconditionally sets meta.sleeperDataReady = True at :3259. GET /api/data?view=app&leagueKey=dynasty_new returns sleeperDataReady:true AND sleeperLoadedLeagueKey:"dynasty_main" simultaneously — a combination the documented contract says cannot occur. The block reports leagueId 1320092771247222784 and 10 real teams (correct) alongside num_teams 12, 58 roster slots and dynasty_main's 141-key IDP scoring card (all wrong; the real league is 10 teams, 27 slots, 48 keys, no IDP). useTeam.js:84-94 reads the flag: true -> leagueMismatch false -> the data-not-ready state that exists precisely for this case never renders.

reproduction.expected: sleeperDataReady:false (per the documented contract) OR a sleeper block whose scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings belong to dynasty_new
reproduction.actual: sleeperDataReady:true with num_teams 12, 58 roster slots, rec 0.08 and idp_sack 2.92 — dynasty_main's values under dynasty_new's leagueId and leagueName

userImpact: On /trade, /waivers and /rosters under dynasty_new the starter/bench split comes from sleeper.rosterPositions (frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:105), so the user is shown a 21-slot IDP lineup with 3 DL / 3 LB / 3 DB / 1 K starting slots for a league that has none of those positions, plus 37 bench slots for a 17-bench league — and the 'no roster data yet' banner that would have prevented all of it is suppressed.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A19-F20 and PRIOR-A21-F05 report the same class (hardcoded league context leaking across leagues) in ROS/public-league; this is the contract-level source those inherit from.

whatWorks: The no-overlay fallback path directly below (server.py:3288-3298) does it correctly: it nulls the sleeper block and sets sleeperDataReady:false. The defect is only on the overlay-succeeded branch.
rootCause: The overlay merge treats 'we fetched the requested league's rosters' as equivalent to 'the sleeper block is valid for the requested league', but the overlay only supplies teams/trades/waivers — scoringSettings, rosterPositions and leagueSettings are never overlaid and silently retain the loaded league's values.
requiredRepair: On the sleeper_matches=False branch, either drop scoringSettings/rosterPositions/leagueSettings from the carried-forward key list (leaving them absent rather than wrong) and keep sleeperDataReady:false, or fetch the requested league's own config in the overlay so the block is genuinely that league's. Do not stamp sleeperDataReady:true unless every field in the block belongs to the requested league.
dependencies: W18-F001 — with a correct scoringProfile this path would 503 before reaching the overlay.

title: src/nfl_data/realized_points.py disagrees with the league host on 36% of player-weeks: it never reads the six reception-distance rules, maps pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost to nflverse columns that no longer exist, and has no kicker scoring at all
claimUnderTest: src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py:6 — 'compute_weekly_points ... is already the single source of truth for Sleeper-format fantasy scoring'. CLAUDE.md — BDVM's baseline is 'realized nflverse PPG under the league's exact scoring'.
observed: Scored 636 real 2025 player-weeks (nflverse rows) against the same 636 Sleeper host stat lines under the SAME live dynasty_main scoring_settings. Only 406 (63.8%) agree within 0.011. Three independent causes, each confirmed by decomposing individual players: (1) rec_0_4/rec_5_9/rec_10_19/rec_20_29/rec_30_39/rec_40p appear in neither _SIMPLE_KEYS nor the threshold-bonus list, costing 157.03 points across 197 rows — Stefon Diggs 2025 wk5 exact 30.100 vs realized 23.400, delta -6.700 = 0.34+4.02+2.34 exactly. (2) _SIMPLE_KEYS maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; the 2025 unified nflverse release names them passing_interceptions, sacks_suffered and fumbles_lost_total, so stat_row.get returns None -> _num -> 0.0 and the key is skipped. Patrick Mahomes wk14 exact 0.823 vs realized 14.823, delta exactly +14.000 = 3 INT x 4.00 + 2 sacks x 1.00. Across the sample these three penalties are worth 208 points that are never charged. (3) No kicker key is read at all (fgm_yds 0.07, xpm 2.31, xpmiss -3.15, six fgmiss_* bands) although K is a starting slot; every kicker scores 0.000 (33/33 rows wrong, mean -9.251). Per-group agreement: IDP 312/350 (89.1%, mean -0.034 — this path is essentially correct), other 66/71, WR 11/64, TE 10/48, RB 4/32, QB 3/38 (mean +6.533), K 0/33 (mean -9.251).

reproduction.expected: 636/636 agree within 0.011 (the tolerance src/league_intel/scorer.py's own docstring sets)
reproduction.actual: 406/636 agree; QB mean +6.533, K mean -9.251, WR mean -1.558

inputs.reference: src/league_intel/scorer.score_stat_line, itself validated 1339/1339 vs Sleeper players_points

userImpact: The direction is systematic, not random: QBs are over-scored by ~6.5 pts/week and pass-catchers under-scored by 0.8-1.6 pts/week, so any fundamental value built on this engine tilts the board toward QBs and away from WR/TE/RB. On /rankings the 'Fund gap' column and on /bdvm the entire value board are derived from it; on /league-comparison the positional-balance verdict a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs is computed from the engine that over-pays QBs.

priorFinding.note: Confirms the reception-band half exactly (6 rules, WR most affected) and extends it with two causes that audit did not report: three dead nflverse column mappings worth +208 pts of uncharged QB penalties, and the complete absence of kicker scoring in a league that starts a K. Also partially confirms PRIOR-A24-F19 and refutes the implication in PRIOR-A22-F02 that IDP is the broken half — measured, IDP is the ONE group this engine gets right.

whatWorks: The IDP path is correct and well-defended: the _SCORING_KEY_ALIASES derivation from sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES resolves idp_pass_def->idp_pd and idp_qb_hit->idp_hit, _tackle_view reconstructs gamebook solo from the post-2025 columns, and the group agrees with the host at 89.1% with mean signed error -0.034.
rootCause: realized_points is an allow-list engine keyed on nflverse column names, in a codebase that also contains a scoring-key-agnostic dot-product engine (src/league_intel/scorer.py) that is provably exact. The allow-list silently degrades in two ways — a live scoring rule with no entry, and an entry whose column was renamed — and _num(None) -> 0.0 makes both indistinguishable from 'the player did nothing'.
requiredRepair: Add rec_0_4..rec_40p (nflverse publishes no reception-depth split, so they must come from src/nfl_data/reception_depth.py or be reported as uncovered, not silently zero); repoint pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost at passing_interceptions/sacks_suffered/fumbles_lost_total via the existing candidate-tuple mechanism; add the kicker family. Structurally: make the engine assert that every NONZERO key in the league's scoring_settings is either mapped or explicitly declared uncoverable, and surface the uncovered set on the payload (src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already exists for this and is not consulted at scoring time).
dependencies: None. src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already enumerates the gap.

title: /api/player/{id}/realized returns reason:'unmapped_player' for every player because it reads a players directory key the sleeper block does not have, and the PlayerPopup that now calls it 404s on the Next origin
claimUnderTest: server.py:11213 — 'What kept the row-filter bug below invisible was not the flag but the absence of a caller: nothing in the frontend requests this.' The 2026-07-27 fix comment at :11271-11288 claims the endpoint now matches rows correctly.
observed: Two independent failures, both live. (a) server.py:11264 does players_dir = sleeper_block.get('players') or sleeper_block.get('playerDict'). The contract's sleeper block has neither key — its actual keys are idToPlayer, playerIds, positions, rosterPositions, scoringSettings, leagueSettings, teams, trades, waivers, tradeWindow*, overlay*. players_dir is therefore always None, unified_mapper.resolve_player(None, ...) returns None, and the route short-circuits to reason:'unmapped_player' with an empty weeks list for every player id — verified for 5849 (Kyler Murray), 9756, 10891 and 6794. The weekly stats DO load (19,421 nflverse rows for 2025 in this container), which is why the response is 'unmapped_player' and not 'no_stats_available'. Even if a directory were passed, idToPlayer is {id: name} and carries no gsis_id, so the `not resolved.gsis_id` guard would still fire. (b) The claim that nothing calls it is now false: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:397 fetches /api/player/{id}/realized — but there is no bridge route under frontend/app/api/player/, so on the production origin (:3000) the request returns HTTP 404 (an HTML page), res.ok is false, and the RealizedPointsSection silently renders nothing. (c) Separately, line 11234 reads latest_contract_data['sleeper'] directly rather than the league it just resolved at :11229, so a non-default leagueKey would be scored with the loaded league's settings.

reproduction.expected: a weeks array scored under the league's settings for a rostered player

userImpact: The 'Realized points — scored on your league's settings' panel on the player popup never appears for any player. The user is not shown a wrong number; they are shown nothing, with no indication the feature exists. Low severity precisely because the section self-suppresses.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A22-F02 says 'never fetches defensive stats, so every IDP player silently returns zero weeks'. Measured, the route returns zero weeks for EVERY player of every position, and the cause is upstream of stat selection (players_dir is None). PRIOR-A22-F03 and PRIOR-A21-F16 ('scores against whatever league's contract happens to be loaded') are CONFIRMED at server.py:11234 but are moot while (a) holds.

whatWorks: The feature flag, auth gate, league resolution and nflverse fetch all work; _rp.compute_cumulative_points is reached with a well-formed empty row list.
rootCause: The route was written against a sleeper-block shape that the contract does not produce, and the in-code comment asserting no caller exists went stale when PlayerPopup added one without a Next bridge route.
requiredRepair: Resolve the player through a directory that carries gsis_id (src/identity/unified_mapper's own override/config layer, or the scraper's player master) rather than sleeper_block['players']; add frontend/app/api/player/[sleeperId]/realized/route.js; and read the sleeper block for the resolved league, not latest_contract_data, at server.py:11234.
dependencies: W18-F003 — once this route returns rows, it will return rows computed by the defective engine.

title: /api/league-comparison benchmarks a hardcoded Sleeper league that is not in the registry, and its per-position sample sizes are hardcoded to a lineup that is not this league's (TE 12 against 24 real TE starters, IDP 96 against 108)
claimUnderTest: src/league_comparison/sleeper_scoring.py:3 — 'This module deliberately bypasses src.api.league_registry because the league-comparison feature only needs scoring rules'. CLAUDE.md — 'never read os.getenv("SLEEPER_LEAGUE_ID") in new code' / all league resolution goes through the registry.
observed: config/league_comparison.json pins my_league to Sleeper id 1312736351547850752, a league named 'Scoring' that does not appear in config/leagues/registry.json. Fetched live: it is a 12-team 2026 league whose 141-key scoring_settings are currently byte-identical to dynasty_main's (diff is empty), but whose roster_positions are NOT — 55 slots with TE1, DL2, LB2, DB2 and IDP_FLEX2, against dynasty_main's 58 slots with TE2, DL3, LB3, DB3 and IDP_FLEX0. Nothing binds the clone to the real league: a commissioner edit to dynasty_main leaves /api/league-comparison silently benchmarking the stale copy. Separately, sample_sizes in the same file are hardcoded {QB 24, RB 24, WR 36, TE 12, FLEX 96, IDP_TOTAL 96}; for a 12-team league starting TE2 the replacement-level cohort should be 24, and starting DL3+LB3+DB3 it should be 108. The live payload confirms both: meta.sampleSizes.TE = 12, meta.myLeague.id = 1312736351547850752. The IDP half of the page is a declared placeholder ('IDP comparison is scaffolded but not yet enabled').

reproduction.expected: myLeague.id == 1312006700437352448 (the registry's dynasty_main) and TE sample size 24

userImpact: The 'TE replacement level' and the TE share-of-value the page reports are measured at TE12 in a league that starts 24 TEs, so the page understates how deep the user must draft at TE and overstates elite-TE scarcity relative to the real lineup. The scoring half of the comparison is currently correct only by coincidence.

priorFinding.note: Confirms 'scoringFit and receptionFit are measured against a Sleeper league that is not in the registry' and names the league (1312736351547850752, 'Scoring'). Adds the independent sample-size defect, which that finding does not cover, and the measured fact that the clone's SCORING currently matches exactly while its LINEUP does not.

whatWorks: The scoring values themselves currently agree with dynasty_main byte-for-byte, and sleeper_scoring._scoring_hash already stamps a content hash of each league's card — the mechanism that would detect divergence exists and is computed, it is simply never compared against the registry league.
rootCause: A second, file-based league identity was introduced alongside the registry rather than through it, and lineup-derived constants were frozen into the same file instead of being read from roster_positions.
requiredRepair: Point my_league at the registry's default league id (or resolve it through league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id) and derive sample_sizes from team_count x roster_positions rather than storing them.

title: /draft's roster-gap panel uses a hardcoded, league-blind position-minimums table, so it reports DL/LB/DB shortages in a league that has no IDP starting slots
claimUnderTest: draft-logic.js:2434 — 'Values chosen to fit a 2-QB/2-RB/3-WR/1-TE + flex IDP starter shape common in SF leagues — adjust via options when a league's shape differs significantly.'
observed: DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS = {QB 3, RB 4, WR 5, TE 2, DL 3, LB 3, DB 3} is a module constant. frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:3685 calls computeRosterBreakdown(rosterPlayers, allPlayersArray) with no third argument, so the default is used verbatim on every render for every league. The stated shape ('1 TE') is already wrong for dynasty_main, which starts TE2 per the live host — a TE minimum of 2 leaves zero bench depth at a position the league starts two of. For dynasty_new the host publishes roster_positions with zero DL, LB and DB slots, yet the panel will still flag those three as needs. The frontend has the correct data available: lib/starter-slots.js exists specifically to expand the league's own rosterPositions, and useTeam() already returns rosterSettings.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'computeRosterBreakdown(' frontend/app/draft/page.jsx && sed -n '2439,2447p' frontend/lib/draft-logic.js && curl -s https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/1320092771247222784 | python3 -c "import json,sys;from collections import Counter;print(Counter(json.load(sys.stdin)['roster_positions']))"
reproduction.expected: position minimums derived from the active league's roster_positions
reproduction.actual: constant {QB:3,RB:4,WR:5,TE:2,DL:3,LB:3,DB:3} for both leagues; dynasty_new host roster_positions contains no DL/LB/DB at all

numericProof.formula: shortage = max(0, positionMins[pos] - rostered[pos]); a league with 0 starting slots at pos must yield shortage 0

userImpact: A user drafting in 'Blood, Sweat, and Beers' is told they need 9 more defensive players in a league that cannot start one, and a dynasty_main user is told a 2-TE cushion is sufficient for a lineup that starts 2 TEs every week.

priorFinding.note: Same class as 'nine other call sites hardcode the dynasty_main lineup', but that finding is scoped to src/trade/. This is the frontend instance and it is not the dynasty_main lineup either — the constant matches no configured league.

whatWorks: computeRosterBreakdown already accepts a positionMins override; the plumbing needed for the fix is present and unused.
rootCause: A single-league heuristic constant survived the multi-league migration because the only caller never passes the override the API offers.
requiredRepair: Derive positionMins from expandStarterSlots(rosterSettings.starters) / sleeper.rosterPositions at the /draft call site, and drop positions the league does not start.

title: src/scoring/baseline_config.py and the twelve other scoring-adjustment symbols the production scraper imports are never called — a fourth scoring constant set that reaches no live path
claimUnderTest: Dynasty Scraper.py imports build_default_baseline_config, build_league_scoring_config, bucket_rule_contributions, compare_to_baseline, persist_scoring_delta_map, compute_profile_features, infer_archetype, build_scoring_tags, build_player_scoring_adjustment, choose_final_multiplier, compute_sample_size_score, run_scoring_backtest and persist_scoring_config inside a try/except, implying the scraper applies scoring-delta adjustments.
observed: All thirteen symbols appear exactly twice in Dynasty Scraper.py — once in the import list and once in the except-branch that nulls them. Grep for '<name>(' returns zero call sites for every one of them. BASELINE_SCORING_MAP itself is a fourth, mutually inconsistent scoring card (pass_yd 0.04, pass_td 4.0, rec 1.0, idp_sack 4.0, idp_tkl_solo 1.5, bonus_rec_te 0.5) and correctly labels itself 'Baseline is a comparison environment only. It is not the live league.' Its only non-test consumer is src/consensus_edge/scoring_fit.py:160, and consensus_edge is flag-off by default per ADR-023. Note also that its key vocabulary (idp_hit, idp_pd, bonus_pass_td_50+) is the pre-alias spelling, not the live league's (idp_qb_hit, idp_pass_def).

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && for f in build_default_baseline_config build_league_scoring_config compare_to_baseline persist_scoring_delta_map build_player_scoring_adjustment run_scoring_backtest; do echo "$f mentions=$(grep -c $f 'Dynasty Scraper.py') calls=$(grep -c \"$f(\" 'Dynasty Scraper.py')"; done
reproduction.expected: at least one call site per imported symbol

numericProof.formula: count(symbol : call sites in Dynasty Scraper.py > 0)

userImpact: None directly — it is dead weight. The risk is to the next reader: the import block is the strongest available signal that the scraper applies scoring adjustments, and it does not, so a fix aimed at the live board could be applied here and change nothing.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A24-F19 concerns RULE_META coverage inside this package; the fact that the package's entry points are unreachable from the scraper is not in the prior set.

whatWorks: baseline_config.py is honest about itself in a docstring, and the map is never mistaken for live scoring by anything that runs.
rootCause: An adjustment pipeline was wired at the import layer and the call sites were either never added or later removed, leaving the imports behind.
requiredRepair: Delete the unused import block from Dynasty Scraper.py (or restore the call sites), and label src/scoring/baseline_config.py's status in CLAUDE.md's directory map so it is not mistaken for a live scoring source.

title: refresh_snapshot's drift filter omits daily_waivers_last_ran, so a pure in-season bookkeeping counter reports as league-rule drift and writes a spurious dated snapshot
claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/config.py:244-249 — 'Drift diffs are scoped to behavior-relevant payload fields ... so chatter (last_message_id etc.) never reads as drift', with _SETTINGS_NOISE_KEYS = {leg, last_scored_leg, last_report}.
observed: Diffing the stored 2026-07-26 snapshot against the live host today produces exactly one settings difference: daily_waivers_last_ran 26 -> 4. That key is Sleeper's counter for which daily-waiver run last executed; it changes every waiver day and encodes no league rule. It is not in _SETTINGS_NOISE_KEYS, so LeagueConfigDrift.has_drift is True and refresh_snapshot(write=True) writes a new sleeper_league_snapshot_<today>.json into config/league_intel/ — which then becomes the file find_latest_snapshot returns. Because the counter moves on a fixed cadence, this will recur indefinitely, accumulating snapshots and producing drift reports that reviewers learn to ignore.

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/repro.sh   # section R2 shows scoring drift {} and roster_positions equal True; then: python3 -c "import json;s=json.load(open('config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json'))['settings'];l=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/sleeper_league_1312006700437352448.json'))['settings'];print({k:(s.get(k),l.get(k)) for k in set(s)|set(l) if s.get(k)!=l.get(k)})"
reproduction.expected: {} — no drift, because no rule changed

userImpact: None to a user. It degrades the operator's drift signal: the one mechanism that would announce a real commissioner scoring change cries wolf on a schedule.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers src/league_intel/config.py's drift filter.

whatWorks: Everything else about the refresh path: the diff is correctly scoped to scoring_settings/roster_positions/settings/status/season/total_rosters, the stored snapshot is never overwritten, and build_config_from_snapshot validates the live payload before it is allowed to become the newest file.
rootCause: _SETTINGS_NOISE_KEYS was written from the keys that were noisy at the time and never extended to the daily-waiver counters.
requiredRepair: Add daily_waivers_last_ran (and, for safety, the other run-state counters) to _SETTINGS_NOISE_KEYS.

title: The canonical league config for dynasty_main is byte-exact against the live Sleeper host: 141/141 scoring keys, 58/58 roster slots and 51/51 settings match, and all 38 published scoring values and 14 published league facts verify
claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/config.py:3 — 'Single source of truth for what the league's rules actually are: scoring settings (every Sleeper key, verbatim)' and 'The two must agree — tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py pins that.'
observed: Every claim holds for dynasty_main. Full key-by-key matrix built at docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/scoring-matrix.csv: 222 rows, 213 MATCH, 7 NOT-MODELLED (fields the registry deliberately does not carry: IR size, playoff teams/week/type, median game, waiver type, FAAB budget), 2 non-MATCH (the daily_waivers_last_ran counter of W18-F008, and the scoringProfile label of W18-F010). Verified: 141/141 scoring keys identical across host, stored snapshot and the live contract's sleeper block; roster_positions identical (QB1 RB2 WR3 TE2 FLEX2 SUPER_FLEX1 K1 DL3 LB3 DB3 + 37 BN = 58, IDP_FLEX 0); 12 teams; best_ball 1; taxi_slots 0; reserve_slots 0; playoff_teams 7, playoff_week_start 15, playoff_type 1, playoff_round_type 0; league_average_match 1 (median game ON); waiver_type 2 with waiver_budget 100 (FAAB); trade_deadline week 13; 3 divisions; 6 draft rounds. All 38 published scoring rates verify exactly, including pass_yd 0.033333=1/30, the six reception-distance bonuses, bonus_fd_qb 0.67 vs bonus_fd_rb/wr/te 1.00, and the full 15-key IDP card with the three 1/9 return-yard rates. The frontend holds NO copy of the scoring settings and derives lineup shape from the contract's sleeper.rosterPositions via frontend/lib/starter-slots.js, so there is nothing there to drift.

reproduction.expected: scoring drift {} and roster_positions equal True
reproduction.actual: scoring drift {} ; roster_positions equal True ; 141 keys / 58 slots / 12 teams on both sides

userImpact: None — this is the part that is right, and it is the foundation everything else in this workstream is measured against.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding asserts or refutes the accuracy of the stored snapshot against the live host; this is the first live verification.

whatWorks: The whole dynasty_main config path: dated-snapshot discovery, _coerce_scoring's required-key canary, the total_rosters vs num_teams cross-check, and the live contract's sleeper block carrying the same 141 keys through to the API. tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py genuinely un-neutralizes the registry (monkeypatched LEAGUE_REGISTRY_PATH plus a direct file read) and pins registry rosterSettings against the snapshot, so this agreement is CI-enforced — for dynasty_main only.
requiredRepair: Extend the same pinning to dynasty_new, which has no snapshot and no equivalent test (see W18-F011).

title: ADR-006's 'pure dot product, no stacking rules' claim independently reproduced against 1,339 host-scored player-weeks (max |delta| 0.005), and stacking answered on real host stat lines: pick-six charges -6.00, distance bonuses stack on the base reception, and one sack pays eight IDP categories
claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/scorer.py:3-25 — 'a pure dot product over the keys shared between a player's weekly stat line and the league's scoring_settings ... No exclusions, no de-duplication, no special-casing ... reproduced Sleeper's own players_points exactly (|delta| <= 0.011) for 1,415 of 1,415 rostered player-weeks.'
observed: Reproduced independently, not inherited. Fetched the 2025 predecessor league (1180092661344120832) with its own scoring_settings plus GET /v1/league/.../matchups/{5,9,14} for host-awarded players_points and GET /v1/stats/nfl/regular/2025/{5,9,14} for the raw stat lines. score_stat_line reproduces the host on 1,339 of 1,339 player-weeks with max |delta| = 0.005, inside the module's own 0.011 tolerance. Stacking, answered from host stat lines rather than from docs: (1) PICK-SIX STACKS — the host emits pass_int and pass_int_td on the same line (3 real cases, e.g. player 4046 wk5: pass_int 1.0, pass_int_td 1.0), so under 2026 rates a pick-six costs -4.00 AND -2.00 = -6.00. (2) RECEPTION-DISTANCE BONUSES STACK ON THE BASE RECEPTION — the buckets partition the receptions (rec_0_4 + rec_5_9 + rec_10_19 + rec_20_29 + rec_30_39 + rec_40p == rec) and are paid in addition to rec x 0.08; an 8-catch line at 1/3/3/0/1/0 scores 0.64 + 4.61 = 5.25 before yardage. (3) ONE SACK PAYS EVERYTHING APPLICABLE — 194 host lines carry idp_sack together with idp_sack_yd, idp_tkl_solo, idp_tkl_ast, idp_tkl_loss, idp_qb_hit and often idp_ff / idp_fum_rec. Worked case (player 4967, wk5, 2026 rates): ff 4.25 + fum_rec 3.19 + qb_hit 2.13 + sack 2.92 + sack_yd 1.111 + tkl_ast 0.80 + tkl_loss 4.25 + tkl_solo 1.33 = 19.981. The host also emits idp_tkl (combined), which carries no rate in this league, so solo+assist are not double-counted — a league that DID set idp_tkl would triple-count, and that would be Sleeper's behaviour too.

numericProof.formula: points = sum over k in (stat_line & scoring_settings) of stat_line[k] * scoring_settings[k]

userImpact: None — this establishes which engine in the repo is correct, and therefore what every other engine must be measured against.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding tests ADR-006. Establishing it is what makes W18-F003's 36% disagreement attributable to realized_points rather than to an unknown.

whatWorks: score_stat_line is exact, pure, deterministic and vocabulary-agnostic — it needs no per-rule mapping and cannot silently drop a live scoring rule. It is also, by grep, reachable from exactly one non-test caller (src/league_intel/sim_calibration.py); the engine wired to the live routes and to BDVM is the allow-list one in src/nfl_data/realized_points.py.
requiredRepair: Consider making score_stat_line the scoring core and reducing realized_points to a nflverse-row -> Sleeper-stat-key normalizer, so that adding a scoring rule stops requiring a code change.

title: The registry's dynasty_new entry is wrong against its own live host on every roster field it models, and models neither the WRRB_FLEX slot the league actually uses nor IR — and no test or snapshot covers it
claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/config.py:10-14 — 'the registry stays the lightweight per-league pointer used for routing and roster-shape consumers ... The two must agree — tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py pins that.' /api/leagues serves rosterSettings to the frontend as fact.
observed: Fetched the live host for dynasty_new (1320092771247222784) read-only. Every roster field the registry models is wrong: rosterSize 24 vs 27 real slots; taxiSize 5 vs taxi_slots 3; starters FLEX 2 vs a host lineup of FLEX 1 + WRRB_FLEX 1. The registry has no vocabulary for WRRB_FLEX at all, so the second flex is served to the frontend as an RB/WR/TE slot when the host restricts it to RB/WR — a TE placed there is not a legal starter. reserve_slots 3 (this league DOES have IR, unlike dynasty_main) is not modelled anywhere. bestBall is absent from the entry and the host says best_ball 0, so the default happens to be right by luck. /api/leagues serves all of this verbatim. tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py pins ONLY dynasty_main (its _registry_main helper selects key == 'dynasty_main'), and there is no config/league_intel snapshot for dynasty_new, so nothing in the 5,867-test suite compares this entry to anything.

reproduction.command: curl -s https://api.sleeper.app/v1/league/1320092771247222784 | python3 -c "import json,sys;from collections import Counter;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print('slots',len(d['roster_positions']),Counter(d['roster_positions']));print({k:d['settings'][k] for k in ('num_teams','taxi_slots','reserve_slots','best_ball')})" ; python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('config/leagues/registry.json'))['leagues'][1]['rosterSettings'])"
reproduction.actual: registry rosterSize 24, taxiSize 5, starters {QB1,RB2,WR3,TE1,FLEX2,SFLEX1}; WRRB_FLEX and IR unmodelled

userImpact: Every roster-shape consumer for this league is off: /rosters splits starters from bench using a 24-slot lineup against a 27-slot roster (3 real players fall off the end), the taxi squad is shown as 5 when it is 3, and a TE can be recommended into a slot the host will not let it start in.

priorFinding.note: The prior set covers dynasty_main's registry correction (test_registry_consumers.py's own docstring records it) but contains no finding that dynasty_new's entry was never given the same treatment.

whatWorks: The registry loader, alias resolution and /api/leagues serialization are all correct — they faithfully serve whatever the file says. src/bdvm/league_config.py already prefers the contract's sleeper block over the registry and calls rosterSettings 'advisory and known to drift', which is the correct posture.
rootCause: dynasty_new was added to the registry by hand and never validated against its own host; the test that would have caught it is hardcoded to dynasty_main and there is no snapshot for the second league.
requiredRepair: Capture a config/league_intel snapshot for dynasty_new (config.py's snapshot machinery is per-league-id already), extend test_registry_consumers.py to loop over every registry entry instead of selecting dynasty_main, and add WRRB_FLEX / REC_FLEX and a reserveSize field to the registry's roster vocabulary (src/bdvm/league_config._FLEX_SLOTS already knows WRRB_FLEX and REC_FLEX; frontend/lib/starter-slots.js does not).
dependencies: W18-F001 and W18-F002 — a correct dynasty_new config is prerequisite to serving that league correctly at all.
